observation_summary: The LookupTranslator fails to correctly translate CharSequence inputs that are not Strings (e.g., CharBuffer) because it relies on Map lookups that fail due to inconsistent equals/hashCode implementations across different CharSequence types.
reasoning_summary: The defect is fundamentally an algorithmic failure in how the translator performs lookups. It assumes that any CharSequence can be used as a key in a HashMap, which is incorrect because CharSequence implementations (like CharBuffer) do not guarantee equality with Strings. The fix requires changing the lookup strategy (e.g., by converting keys to Strings or using a different data structure/comparison logic) to correctly handle the input, which is a procedural/algorithmic correction.
evidence_used: The core of org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate is a HashMap<CharSequence, CharSequence> lookupMap.
It is therefore inappropriate to use arbitrary CharSequence instances as elements in a set or as keys in a map.
A char buffer is not equal to any other type of object.
The lookup on a CharBuffer in the Map will always fail when compared against the String implementations that it contains.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the issue involves the CharSequence interface, the root cause is the internal implementation choice of using a HashMap with keys that don't support consistent equality, rather than a mismatch in the method signature or contract between two components.
This is not a missing capability or a design-level omission; the translator exists and works for Strings, but its internal lookup algorithm is flawed for other CharSequence types.
